- Model consistently overestimates early in the 30-day horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later days.
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and overshoot after sharp spikes in true values (e.g., 70→75+).
- Mean reversion is under-predicted: model fails to anticipate sharp downward corrections after upward spikes.
- Model lags behind true trend reversals, especially in the 15–25 day window.
- Forecasts show persistent bias toward lower values in the final 5–10 days of the 30-day window.
- Model underestimates true values when the 30-day history contains recent high volatility or sharp upward moves.
- Overshoot correction: if true value exceeds forecast by >5%, reduce next forecast by 2–3% to avoid overcorrection.
- Lag correction: if true value is >10% above forecast at day 10–15, adjust forecast downward by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- Mean reversion trigger: if forecast > true value by >3% for 3 consecutive days, reduce forecast by 1% per day until alignment.
- Horizon-specific: last 5 days of forecast should be adjusted upward if true values show upward momentum in the prior 10 days.
